entities.name: Priesthood of Amun
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary: The most powerful religious institution in ancient Egypt, centered at the great temple complex of Karnak in Thebes. During the New Kingdom (c. 1550–1070 BCE), the priesthood of Amun controlled vast estates, enormous wealth, and wielded political influence rivaling or exceeding that of the pharaoh. The High Priest of Amun effectively ruled Upper Egypt during the late New Kingdom. Akhenaten's religious revolution was partly motivated by desire to break Amun's priestly monopoly. The institution persisted for over a millennium, accumulating texts, administering temple economies, and conducting elaborate rituals that generated much of the surviving Egyptian religious corpus.
